summary: 多项送花实验观察收花后的情绪和社交反应。研究者进而提出一个演化假说：花朵给人带来的愉悦，也可能帮助植物获得人类栽培。

sentences: Why do we give people flowers?
为什么我们给人花？
To offer condolence to those who are grieving.
向哀伤的人们表示哀悼。
To celebrate.
庆祝。
To woo.
来呼唤
To ask for forgiveness.
请求宽恕
We all know intuitively that there is a universal emotional response.
我们都直觉地知道，有一种普遍的情感反应。
In the US alone, the flower industry is now worth about $5 billion a year, which suggests that, at the very least, they service a compelling human need.
仅在美国，花卉工业现在每年就价值约50亿美元，这说明它们至少服务于迫切的人类需求。

paragraphs.brief: 更愿意敞开心扉谈私事。
sentences: Recent studies at the Department of Psychology at Rutgers State University of New Jersey investigated claims that flowers are unique among living organisms in their ability to induce profound changes in our emotional state.
在新泽西州立大学Rutgers大学心理学系最近进行的研究调查了以下说法：鲜花在活生物体中是独一无二的，能够引起我们情感状态的深刻变化。
As the first part of their research, the Rutgers team visited 150 women in their homes.
作为研究的第一部分，Rutgers小组访问了家中的150名妇女。
Each was presented with a variety of gifts such as flowers, fruit or sweets.
每人都收到各种礼物，如花、水果或糖果。
The women were unaware that the study was about the effect of the flowers on their emotions.
妇女们不知道这项研究是了解花朵对她们情感的影响。
They were told that it was a study about their daily moods, and that they would receive a gift in return for taking part.
他们被告知，这是对他们日常情绪的研究，他们将获得礼物，作为参加学习的回报。
Following the presentation of the gift, those receiving flowers were assessed as displaying a much more positive mood than those who got other gifts, and this effect lasted for several days.
赠送礼物后，那些收花的人被评为比那些得到其他礼物的人更积极得多，这种效果持续了几天。
After receiving flowers, they were also more willing to answer questions concerning their social circle and intimate conversations with friends and family.
收到鲜花后，她们还更愿意回答有关其社会圈子的问题，以及与朋友和家人的亲密交谈。
The results suggest that flowers influence our secondary socio-emotional behaviours, as well as having a strong effect on our immediate emotional expression.
结果显示，花朵影响着我们的次等社会情感行为，并且对我们即时的情感表现产生了强烈的影响。

paragraphs.brief: 在封闭空间拉近陌生人的距离。
sentences: In the second study, the psychologists observed participants being handed single flowers, or alternative gifts, in a constrained and stressful situation – inside an elevator.
在第二项研究中，心理学家观察到，在电梯内，有人在紧张和紧张的情况下，把一束花或其他礼物送给了参加者。
Contrary to predictions regarding gender differences, both men and women presented with flowers were more likely to smile, to stand closer and to initiate conversation.
与关于性别差异的预测相反，男女用鲜花展示更可能微笑、站得更近并开始对话。
Several subjects who were given the alternative gift then learnt that flowers were also being handed out, and returned to the elevator and demanded a flower.
一些接受替代礼物的学员得知，花也送出去了，然后返回电梯，要求送花。
The scientists used elevators for this study precisely because the most typical behaviour in sparsely occupied elevators is for people to retreat to opposite corners.
科学家们使用电梯来进行这项研究恰恰是因为最典型的行为在稀有占用的电梯里是人们撤退到对角。

The subjects who received flowers, however, closed up that space to a considerable extent – indicating that the flowers not only induced a strong positive mood, but brought a significant affiliation among people who had never previously met.
花朵不仅激发了强烈的积极情绪，也给以前从未相遇的人带来了重要的联系关系。

paragraphs.brief: 对鲜花出人意料的强烈反应。
sentences: The third study involved regularly sending flowers to a selected sample of men and women.
第三项研究定期向选定的男女样本送花。
The researchers found not only a profound elevation of mood, but also reliable improvements in other measures of cognitive function, like memory.
研究人员不仅发现情绪高涨而且还发现在认知功能方面有了可靠的改进比如记忆
In this series of experiments, some participants produced such extraordinary emotional displays that the psychologists were totally unprepared for them.
在一系列实验中，一些参与者制作了如此非凡的情感展示，使心理学家完全没有做好准备。
Subjects gave spontaneous hugs and kisses to the people who delivered the flowers, and sent invitations to the psychologists to come to their homes for refreshments.
对象自发地拥抱和亲吻送花的人，并向心理学家发出邀请，请他们回家喝点心。
Various evolutionary hypotheses attempt to explain the remarkably powerful psychological effect of flowers.
各种进化假设试图解释花朵的极大心理影响。
One is that our aesthetic preferences for fertile locations and growing things stem from prehistory, when these clues in our environment could mean the difference between starvation and survival.
一个是，我们对肥沃地方和生长事物的审美偏好源于史前，当我们环境中的这些线索可能意味着饥饿和生存之间的区别。
We may have become hardwired to respond positively to flowers because for early man, finding them in a particular location predicted future food supplies and possibly a better place to rear children.
我们可能已经变得难以对花朵做出积极反应，因为对于早期人来说，在某个地方发现花朵预测了未来的粮食供应，并有可能是抚养孩子的更好地方。
Yet the flaw in this argument is that the showy flowers which humans seem to find most visually attractive are generally found on those plants which yield no edible products.
然而，这一论点的缺点是，人类似乎认为最有视觉吸引力的鲜花通常出现在那些没有可食用产品的植物上。

paragraphs.brief: 鲜花的感官吸引力与实际用途。
sentences: The Rutgers psychologists’ findings show that the various physical attributes of flowers combine to directly affect our emotions through multi-channel interactions.
Rutgers心理学家的研究结果显示，花朵的各种物理特征通过多渠道互动直接影响到我们的感情。
We have evolved preferences for the particular colours, textures, patterned symmetries and specific floral odours which influence our moods.
我们逐渐形成了对特定颜色、质地、模式上的对称以及影响我们情绪的特定植物气味的偏好。
Indeed, previous research has established that popular perfumes, which often have a floral ‘top-note’, will actually reduce depression.
事实上，先前的研究已经确定，流行香水(通常有花朵的“顶点”香水)实际上将减少抑郁症。

The origins of these inclinations may well be as the evolutionary theories suggest: the patterned symmetries of flowers can be detected easily as a recognisable signal within a wide variety of visual arrays, and a response to certain colour tones is important in finding ripe fruit against a leafy background.
这些倾向的起源很可能与进化理论所显示的一样：花朵的图案对称很容易被检测为各种视觉阵列中的可识别信号，对某种色调的反应对于在叶子背景中找到成熟的果实十分重要。
But, claim the Rutgers team, these preferences have long been separated from their primary evolutionary use, and become rewarding to us more generally.
但是，拉特格斯团队，这些偏好已经与它们的主要进化用途分离了很久，并且更普遍地对我们有利。
Thus plants with preferred colours, shapes and odours – despite having no other products – would therefore be protected and dispersed.
因此，尽管没有其他产品，但具有首选颜色、形状和气味的植物将受到保护和分散。
The Rutgers study suggests that flowers may have actually evolved to exploit their peculiar impact on humans.
拉特格斯的研究表明花朵实际上可能已经进化来利用它们对人类的特殊影响
The team’s theory proposes a plant-human co-evolution, or even domestication, based on the intense emotional rewards that flowers provide.
团队的理论提出植物与人类共同进化，甚至将花朵带来强烈的情感回报。

The idea that flowering plants, with no known food or other basic survival value to man, have co-evolved with us by exploiting an emotional niche instead, is very much like the scenario presented for the evolution of dogs.
开花植物对于人类来说没有已知的食物或其他基本生存价值，而通过利用情感优势与我们共同发展，这种想法与狗进化的场景非常相似。
Flowers may be the plant equivalent of ‘companion animals’.
花朵可能相当于 " 伴生动物 "。
If this is true, then there is a very real sense in which, when you next give flowers, they are using you just as much as you are using them.
如果这是真的，那么就有一个非常真实的意义，当你下次送花的时候，他们就像你一样使用花朵。

items.answer: v · Some common social functions of flowers

items.why: 开头列出慰问、庆祝、求爱和致歉，都是日常以花向人表达心意的场合。

items.zh: 为 B 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: iv · Becoming more open about personal matters
items.solution: 更愿意敞开心扉谈私事

items.why: 收到花的女性不只情绪改善，也更肯谈自己的感受与个人话题。

items.zh: 为 C 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: vii · Bridging the gap between strangers in an enclosed space
items.solution: 在封闭空间拉近陌生人的距离
items.cue: 在第二项研究中，心理学家观察到，在电梯内，有人在紧张和紧张的情况下，把一束花或其他礼物送给了参加者。
items.why: 电梯实验中，收花者主动缩短与陌生人的距离，打破通常保持距离的习惯。

items.zh: 为 D 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: ii · Some surprisingly strong responses to flowers
items.solution: 对鲜花出人意料的强烈反应

items.zh: 为 E 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.cue: 然而，这一论点的缺点是，人类似乎认为最有视觉吸引力的鲜花通常出现在那些没有可食用产品的植物上。
items.why: 作者先介绍花朵象征环境肥沃的演化解释，再指出这种解释无法涵盖观察到的偏好。

items.why: 作者区分香气、色彩等本身带来的愉悦，与早期判断环境是否有用的实际功能。

items.en: The study focused on participants’ short-term reaction to receiving flowers.
items.zh: 研究的重点是与会者对收花的短期反应。

items.en: Participants were deliberately misled as to the aim of the study.
items.zh: 有意误导参与者了解研究的目的。

items.en: Receiving flowers had a notable effect on participants’ mental capacities.
items.zh: 接收花朵对参加者的心理能力产生了显著影响。

items.en: Male and female responses were more uniform than expected.
items.zh: 男性和女性的反应比预期的更加一致。

items.en: The presence of flowers might indicate a potential source of ________ in a particular location, and primitive humans would search for such signs when looking for a suitable site to raise their ____ (Q39).

items.why: 原文是“food supplies”,题目限一词，规范填food。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 开头列出慰问、庆祝、求爱和致歉，都是日常以花向人表达心意的场合。
回到对应内容“然而，这一论点的缺点是，人类似乎认为最有视觉吸引力的鲜花通常出现在那些没有可食用产品的植物上”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: “that there is a universal emotional response”补足 know 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 know 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
Several subjects … then learnt that flowers were also being handed out, and returned to the elevator and demanded a flower.
“who were given the alternative gift”修饰前面的 subjects。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 subjects，再把修饰信息接回主句。
